To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for the task of detecting subtle lung nodules, the superior resolution of the selenium-based flat-panel detector provided better detection performance than the cesium-iodide-based detector, even though the noise was greater in the selenium-based detector images.

(1) the detectability of simulated nodules in a lung background is higher for a selenium-based flat-panel detector than for a cesium iodine-based detector, (2) the detectability advantage of the selenium detector is greater for smaller nodules, and (3) the difference in detectability between the selenium and cesium iodide detectors is statistically significant for one nodule size.

(1) the selenium detector had higher detectability than the cesium detector for all three nodule sizes; and (2) the differences in detectability between the detectors were statistically significant for the 2.75-mm nodule.

the physical image quality metrics of resolution and noise have an impact on clinical detection performance for digital radiographic detectors and that the impact is dependent on the specific detector and nodule size.
the physical metrics of resolution and noise are not independent of each other and that the detectability of a nodule is dependent upon the physical metrics as a whole.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, for digital detectors that are used in chest radiography, the higher the resolution and lower the noise, the better the detectability of subtle pulmonary nodules.
for the particular imaging task studied, the selenium detector provided better detectibility than the cesium detector, but the differences between the two detectors were relatively small.
, in general, the higher the resolution of a detector, the higher the detectability of the object of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physical image quality metrics are not sufficient to determine the performance of a digital radiography system for a specific clinical task.
the physical characteristics of a particular radiographic detector can have a significant impact on the detectability performance for specific tasks and should be considered in detector design.
the relationship between physical metrics and clinical performance is not straightforward.
